definitions.explanation: A hard candy, often with herbal or menthol flavoring, sucked to soothe a sore or dry throat.

examples.japanese: のど{飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なめる。
examples.english: I suck on a throat lozenge.
My throat hurts, so I bought some cough drops.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧のど{飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れている→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: The air is dry in winter, so I always pop a throat lozenge before meetings.

notes:
Also written {喉飴|のどあめ}. A lozenge is sucked, so the usual verb is なめる; ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ is also heard, more loosely.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- のど{飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なめる: to suck a throat lozenge
- ⟦ハーブ→ハーブ：11246_haabu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧のど{飴|あめ}: an herbal lozenge
- のど{飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}ち{歩|ある}く→持ち歩く：05739_mochiaruku⟧: to carry lozenges around
